notes: Both raw captures passed all hard five-map, depth, teardown, profiler, viewer, and PVS lifecycle gates.
The ordnance setup temporarily enables mortar/orbital permission on loaded area and roofing components, then restores every value.
The vehicle setup uses 24 damageable occupants: 16 in the tracked passenger set and 8 discoverable only through interior markers.
Collision sound and occupant damage are enabled; wheel and footprint damage are disabled to isolate the interior landing path.

change.ordnance: CMUTopDownOrdnanceSystem accepts a resettable caller-owned result. Only the per-tick orbital firing update reuses one buffer; low-frequency callers retain the allocating API. Resolution still executes on every tick.
change.vehicle: Landing sound and occupant damage share one event-local union/query result. The snapshot is cleared after every landing; footprint targets retain their separate set.
change.damage: Per-victim DamageSpecifier construction remains isolated because target damage events may cancel or customize damage independently.
change.behavior: No cross-tick result cache, invalidation policy, gameplay cap, damage pooling, or target filtering was added.

ordnance.conclusion: The exact allocation was removed while work counts remained identical. P95 did not improve, so no CPU improvement is claimed.

vehicleLanding.conclusion: One exact union/query replaced two while preserving all 24 targets and damage applications. The dominant per-victim damage allocation remains unchanged.

validation.releaseBenchmarksBuild: Passed with zero warnings and zero errors.

resultBufferUnitTest.behavior: Reset changes selection, clears outcome and surfaces, and retains the caller-owned list instance.

deferredRisks: The Bush ordnance permissions are intentionally false in production; the runner temporarily enables them to force the resolution path. A live firing-delay capture remains desirable.
The representative column had three blocking surfaces across five resolved maps; denser or deeper future networks scale with their actual map/surface count.
The synthetic vehicle occupants had no ActorComponent, so global interior audio delivery was not exercised even though collision-sound recipient discovery ran.
Real wheel damage, footprint crush queries, occupants entering/leaving during an event, and a populated production vehicle landing remain live validation risks.
Per-victim damage processing still allocates 12,096 bytes for 24 targets. Pooling mutable specifications could leak target-specific event mutations and was deliberately not introduced.
